facts.text: - Perimeter change: the SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. acquisition closed "On September 1, 2026" and its purchase price allocation is described as "provisional and subject to adjustment during the measurement period" (Q3 statements, note 3, page 7). Evidence to mechanism to consequence: only one month of SECURE is in the Q3 statements, so quarterly and nine-month totals mix pre- and post-acquisition perimeters, and downstream trend or pro forma work needs the separately stated pro forma disclosure ("unaudited consolidated pro forma revenue and loss before income taxes for the nine months ended September 30, 2026") rather than reported totals alone. - Comparative revision: the Q3 statements state "comparative amounts have been revised for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025" and for December 31, 2025 balances (note 3, pages 8 and 9). Evidence to mechanism to consequence: the December 31, 2025 column in 2026 documents differs from the as-originally-reported FY2025 annual statements, which are not supplied, so the original-versus-revised bridge for FY2025 cannot be checked from this pack. - Period conventions of the 2026 filings: the file labels do not equal period or filing date (for example the statements for the three months ended March 31, 2026 carry a file label dated 2026-03-31 but state Board approval on April 29, 2026). Period and basis here come from located content only. - Management measures versus filed statements: Net Leverage uses "Run-Rate EBITDA" that adds management-estimated "Run-Rate EBITDA Adjustments"; it is an attributed management claim and does not override filed statement figures. - Source quality versus extraction: all sources are text extractions of HTML. facts.label: Interpretation (evidence-based, no conclusion on creditworthiness)
facts.text: - Leverage rose with the SECURE closing and the new financing. Reported debt before adjustments grew from 7,426.7 to 11,696.4 while the management leverage ratio moved from 3.4x to 3.8x, because the ratio's denominator includes 730.9 of management run-rate adjustments. On trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA alone, net debt to Adjusted EBITDA is about 5.05x (calculation below), which sits above the 4.50x general covenant level but is not a covenant calculation (covenant definitions are not supplied; the 5.00x step-up applies for four quarters after a Material Acquisition, and whether SECURE qualifies is not stated). - Net loss from continuing operations in the nine months is driven by items below Adjusted EBITDA: foreign exchange loss 196.7, interest and other finance costs 482.9, and an equity-method loss, against Adjusted EBITDA of 1,748.4 (Q3 statements page:1). - Cash generation: operating cash flow less purchase of property and equipment is thin for nine months 2026 (calculation below), and management's Adjusted Free Cash Flow of 484.9 depends on add-backs and a separate "incremental growth investments" addition of 182.4 (Q3 release page:18). - Reported Q3 revenue growth of 27.2% includes the one month of SECURE and other acquisitions; the release states organic growth of 7.4%.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The dominant transaction is the SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. acquisition. The definitive agreement was entered "On April 12, 2026" (Q1 statements note 18, subsequent events); SECURE shareholders approved it in May and it went through regulatory review (Q2 release); GFL acquired 100% of the common shares "On September 1, 2026" (Q3 statements note 3, page:7). Documentary Fact: total consideration of about 5,414.1 satisfied by share capital of 4,334.8 and cash of 1,079.3; SECURE operates waste processing, industrial waste disposal and recycling in Western Canada and North Dakota; initial accounting is provisional and based on historical carrying values, so fair value adjustments could change goodwill, intangibles, property and the 1,006.6 of other long-term liabilities assumed. Mechanism: issuing 77,708,769 subordinate voting shares funded most of the price with equity, which limits the incremental debt, while the cash portion, repayment of acquired debt (if any, not stated in the supplied text) and transaction costs were funded with new debt. Credit implication: the equity-heavy structure moderates leverage growth, but the assumed obligations, closure liabilities of 271.8 and crude oil commitments broaden the senior and structurally senior claims ahead of or alongside the notes.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: collection is the largest service line and pricing is described as "5.7% from core pricing" (Q3 release page:2). Mechanism: route-based collection revenue with pricing above inflation supports revenue visibility and margin resilience, while landfill and transfer volumes depend on construction and industrial activity. Implication: stable operating cash generation supports debt service tolerance, subject to the pricing claim being management's and to customer contract data being absent. 2. Leverage and acquisition integration. Evidence: Net Leverage 3.8x against 3.4x at December 31, 2025 (CP-1 handoff), and an unadjusted net-debt-to-trailing-Adjusted-EBITDA calculation above 5x in CP-1. Mechanism: SECURE contributes one month of EBITDA but all of its debt-funded cost and assumed liabilities, so reported coverage and leverage understate or overstate depending on whether run-rate adjustments of 730.9 are realised. Implication: refinancing and covenant headroom depend on the Material Acquisition step-up and on delivery of run-rate earnings; monitoring posture should be heightened until two full quarters including SECURE are reported. 3. Control and take-private uncertainty. Evidence: Special Committee and November 9, 2026 deadline (Q3 release page:1). Mechanism: a leveraged buyout or sponsor takeover could add debt or trigger change-of-control provisions in notes and credit facilities. Implication: monitoring item; no conclusion without indentures and credit agreements. 4. Cash-flow conversion. Evidence: management Adjusted Free Cash Flow of 484.9 for nine months against unadjusted operating cash flow less capex of 37.3 (CP-1 calculation). Mechanism: large add-backs (transaction costs, CEO remuneration, incremental growth investments) bridge the two. Implication: the committee should read management free cash flow alongside the unadjusted figure. 5. Structural claims. Evidence: closure obligations, performance bonds and letters of credit (Q3 statements page:11, page:18, page:19). Mechanism: asset retirement and surety obligations rank with operating claims and rise with landfill acquisitions. Implication: recovery prospects for unsecured noteholders depend on asset coverage after secured facilities and these obligations; no expected recovery outcome is given.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: GFL Environmental Inc. is a resilient, price-led waste operator whose credit profile has weakened in the near term because the SECURE acquisition lifted carrying debt by CAD 4,248.8 million in nine months and management Net Leverage to 3.8x from 3.4x. The strongest support is steady collection and landfill earnings, with Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 678.7 million, a 31.5% margin, stated covenant compliance and mostly equity-funded purchase consideration. The weakest point is thin unadjusted cash generation: operating cash flow less capital spending was CAD 37.3 million over nine months, and net debt is 5.05x trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA. The outcome depends on SECURE earnings reaching the run-rate management assumes, headroom under the 5.00x acquisition covenant step-up, and the take-private review. The pack cannot confirm any of the three.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. GFL Environmental Inc. changed perimeter on September 1, 2026. SECURE was bought for about CAD 5,414.1 million, of which CAD 4,334.8 million was shares and CAD 1,079.3 million cash, but only one month of SECURE earnings is in the Q3 2026 statements. facts.text: 2. Leverage depends on management estimates. Net Leverage of 3.8x divides CAD 11,399.9 million of net debt by Run-Rate EBITDA of CAD 2,988.0 million, of which CAD 730.9 million (about a quarter) is management adjustment; on trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 2,257.1 million the same net debt is 5.05x. The covenant ceiling is 5.00x for four fiscal quarters after a Material Acquisition and 4.50x otherwise, and covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom cannot be measured. Management guides to Net Leverage "in the mid 3s" by the end of 2026, a forward claim. [CP-1 calculations]

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. First, the business is recurring and vertically integrated: collection is the largest revenue line and landfill and transfer add disposal control, which supports revenue visibility and margin resilience (Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model). Second, earnings momentum is real in the filed figures: Adjusted EBITDA grew in each quarter of 2026 and management raised guidance three times, though guidance is Management Language. Third, the acquisition was paid mainly with equity, issuing 77,708,769 subordinate voting shares, which limits the debt added by SECURE and leaves the revolver largely undrawn on a nominal basis relative to its size (the availability figure is not supplied). Fourth, the maturity profile has no material maturity before 2028 and interest on most notes is fixed in USD, with cross-currency swaps on the newest instruments (Documentary Fact). Fifth, covenant compliance is stated at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact), and disclosure of non-IFRS bridges is detailed each quarter (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. First, leverage on reported earnings is high and rests on run-rate estimates for the stated ratio, so the margin for error against a 5.00x covenant depends on an unsupplied definition (Analyst Interpretation). Second, cash conversion after capital spending and interest is thin and management free cash flow relies on add-backs (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Third, integration risk: provisional purchase accounting, a large goodwill balance (CAD 12,583.1 million, versus CAD 6,894.9 million at December 31, 2025) and a net loss from continuing operations mean book equity is largely acquired intangibles (Documentary Fact). Fourth, the take-private review and a dual-class structure with unspecified voting terms leave control and future leverage policy uncertain (Insufficient Information on voting rights). Fifth, commodity and fuel exposure: diesel is cited as a margin headwind, and the new crude oil commitments add a fixed obligation whose counterparties and tenor are not supplied (Management Language; Documentary Fact). Sixth, foreign exchange: most notes are USD while much revenue is CAD and USD, a mix that moves reported leverage and caused a CAD 196.7 million foreign exchange loss in nine months (Documentary Fact).

Module CP-0 (source readiness) for GFL Environmental Inc. (ticker GFL; Ontario, Canada; foreign private issuer filing Form 40-F and furnishing interim reports and earnings releases on Form 6-K; reporting currency CAD, "$" in the 6-K documents means Canadian dollars unless noted). As-of date: 2026-11-05 (cutoff 2026-11-05). Pathway: credit_snapshot. Current period q3-2026 (three and nine months ended September 30, 2026); prior period fy-2025. Requested downstream modules: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5 (the "minimum" set).

Question answered: can the supplied source set support those modules, and what remains blocked. This module gives no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no investment opinion, and it does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Assertion: SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY.
## Sources

## Findings
### Readiness verdict by consumer
| Consumer | Status | Basis |

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Q3 2026 interim financial statements and release give statements of operations, financial position, cash flows, segments, debt and covenant text for the current period. FY2025 audited annual statements and MD&A are not in the pack (see Gaps G1 and G2). |

| CP-1A | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Same evidence; facility-level debt, interest and cash interest for the latest quarter are located. Maturity ladder, revolver availability and covenant ratio values are not supplied (G3, G4, G5). |

| CP-2 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Discrete Q1, Q2, Q3 and nine-month figures, Adjusted EBITDA reconciliations and segment tables are located. Fiscal year 2025 figures are available only as comparatives or "December 31, 2025" columns inside 2026 interim documents (G1). |

| CP-5 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Latest-quarter movements, guidance and subsequent-period events are located in the Q3 release; the pending take-private review and the SECURE acquisition are narrated only by management. |
No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. No missing downstream analytical handoff is treated as a source condition.
### Usable coverage

- The 40-F is a cover and incorporation-by-reference document. Its text states the annual information form is "filed as Exhibit 99.1", the MD&A as "Exhibit 99.2" and the audited statements as "Exhibit 99.3". None of those exhibits is in the supplied text, so the 40-F supports identity, listing, share counts and filing status only: "At December 31, 2025, 346,110,312 subordinate voting shares, 11,812,964 multiple voting shares, 4,867,006 Series A perpetual convertible preferred shares and 8,196,721 Series B perpetual convertible preferred shares were issued and outstanding."

- The three interim financial statement exhibits (Q1, Q2, Q3 2026) are filed financial reports and control reported figures. The three earnings releases are management documents; their IFRS tables repeat the statements and their non-IFRS tables (Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Free Cash Flow, Net Leverage, Run-Rate EBITDA) are attributed management measures.

- Q3 statements (source 21de76c7...): statement of operations (page 1), financial position (page 2), cash flows (pages 3 and 4), note 7 long-term debt (pages 11 to 13), note 8 interest (pages 13 and 14), note 11 operating segments with Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (pages 14 to 16), note 15 commitments including letters of credit and performance bonds (page 18 and 19). Quote located: "The Total Net Funded Debt to Adjusted EBITDA ratio to be maintained is equal to or less than 5.00 to 1.00 for a period of four complete fiscal quarters following completion of a Material Acquisition and at all other times, equal to or less than 4.50 to 1.00."

- Q3 release (source ee28f5cf...): guidance, Net Leverage table and non-IFRS reconciliations (pages 2, 3, 10 to 18). Quote located: "Net Leverage2 is estimated to be in the mid 3s by the end of 2026."
### Strongest contrary evidence and limitations

- Perimeter change: the SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. acquisition closed "On September 1, 2026" and its purchase price allocation is described as "provisional and subject to adjustment during the measurement period" (Q3 statements, note 3, page 7). Evidence to mechanism to consequence: only one month of SECURE is in the Q3 statements, so quarterly and nine-month totals mix pre- and post-acquisition perimeters, and downstream trend or pro forma work needs the separately stated pro forma disclosure ("unaudited consolidated pro forma revenue and loss before income taxes for the nine months ended September 30, 2026") rather than reported totals alone.

- Comparative revision: the Q3 statements state "comparative amounts have been revised for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025" and for December 31, 2025 balances (note 3, pages 8 and 9). Evidence to mechanism to consequence: the December 31, 2025 column in 2026 documents differs from the as-originally-reported FY2025 annual statements, which are not supplied, so the original-versus-revised bridge for FY2025 cannot be checked from this pack.

- Period conventions of the 2026 filings: the file labels do not equal period or filing date (for example the statements for the three months ended March 31, 2026 carry a file label dated 2026-03-31 but state Board approval on April 29, 2026). Period and basis here come from located content only.

- Management measures versus filed statements: Net Leverage uses "Run-Rate EBITDA" that adds management-estimated "Run-Rate EBITDA Adjustments"; it is an attributed management claim and does not override filed statement figures.

- Source quality versus extraction: all sources are text extractions of HTML. Text extraction is not a fidelity review; tables were read as extracted and no image, chart or footnote-marker rendering was inspected.
### Entity and instrument roles located

- Registrant, issuer of the reporting group and parent: GFL Environmental Inc.; subsidiaries consolidated. Borrower and guarantor identities for each debt instrument are not stated in the supplied text, except the tax-exempt bonds: "guaranteed jointly and severally, fully and unconditionally by GFL and certain of its subsidiaries" (note 7). Restricted versus unrestricted subsidiary definitions are not supplied.

- Revolving Credit Agreement "dated as of September 27, 2021 and as amended and restated through September 1, 2026"; Term Loan B Facility entered "On August 28, 2026", maturing "August 28, 2033"; both described as secured by mortgages, a general security agreement and share pledges. The 6.750% 2031 notes: "Collateral securing the 6.750% 2031 Secured Notes has been released ... the notes are no longer secured."
- Non-wholly owned subsidiary stand-alone facilities are included in "Other" debt (note 7).
- Equity-method associate GFL Environmental Services (divested March 1, 2025) with a Call Option carried at fair value; related party transactions in note 16.
### Version relationships

- The Q1, Q2 and Q3 statements and releases are separate periodic documents; none supersedes another. Each release pairs with the same-period statements. No duplicates are present; no hash-identical sources are in the set.

- The Revolving Credit Agreement text moved from "amended and restated through April 29, 2025" (Q1, Q2 statements) to "amended and restated through September 1, 2026" (Q3 statements); the agreement itself and its amendments are not supplied, so these descriptions are the only evidence.
### Source profile coverage notes

- Earnings releases: reported and adjusted figures, reconciliations, quarter and year-to-date columns and guidance are present in each release. Q1 release guidance is dated with the original guidance of February 11, 2026 referenced but not supplied.
- Decks and workbooks: none supplied. No slide, speaker note, chart or workbook coverage is claimed.
- Legal and financing documents: none supplied (context states legal_documents "none"). Indentures, credit agreement and Term Loan B credit agreement are absent.
## Calculations
None. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate. Counts only: 7 issuer sources; pages as stated in the table in Sources (5, 15, 16, 18, 18, 18, 20; 110 pages in total); 0 handoffs.
## Gaps
| ID | Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| G1 | Fiscal year 2025 audited consolidated financial statements, MD&A and annual information form (Exhibits 99.1 to 99.3 of the 40-F) are not in the pack; only the 40-F cover is supplied. FY2025 figures exist only as comparative columns in 2026 documents and are partly revised. Not supplied. | High | CP-1, CP-2 | Supply the 40-F exhibits or the FY2025 earnings release. |

| G2 | No Q4 2025 or full-year 2025 earnings release. The fourth quarter of 2025 discrete figures are Not calculable from supplied text without arithmetic outside CP-0. Trailing twelve months Adjusted EBITDA at December 31, 2025 appears only as a management figure in 2026 releases. | Medium | CP-2, CP-5 | Supply the Q4 2025 release. |

| G3 | Debt maturity schedule by year, including a contractual cash flow table, is not in the interim statements; maturities are available only per instrument in note 7 footnotes. The annual MD&A "Contractual Obligations" section is incorporated by reference in the 40-F but not supplied. Not supplied. | Medium | CP-1A | Supply the FY2025 MD&A or an obligations table. |

| G4 | Revolving credit facility undrawn availability and total liquidity are not stated. Drawn amounts, facility size and letters of credit are stated separately; the split of letters of credit between facilities is partial ("inclusive of letters of credit under both the Revolving Credit Facility and EDC Guaranteed LC Facility"). Not supplied. | Medium | CP-1A, CP-5 | Supply an MD&A liquidity section or lender disclosure. |

| G5 | Actual covenant ratio values are not disclosed; only compliance statements and thresholds are given ("GFL was in compliance with these covenants"). Definitions of "Total Net Funded Debt", "Adjusted EBITDA" for covenant purposes and "Material Acquisition" are in the credit agreement, which is not supplied. Whether the SECURE acquisition triggered the 5.00 to 1.00 step-up is not stated in the supplied text. | High | CP-1A, CP-5 | Supply the Revolving Credit Agreement and compliance certificate data. |

| G6 | Indentures, guarantor structure, ranking, redemption terms, change-of-control provisions and the Term Loan B credit agreement are not supplied; these matter for the pending take-private review. | High | CP-1A, CP-5 | Supply indentures and the credit agreements. |

| G7 | SECURE purchase price allocation is provisional; SECURE standalone financials, financing sources detail and any post-September 30, 2026 acquisition or financing events are not covered by a subsequent-events note in the Q3 statements (no such note appears in the extracted text). Subsequent events are visible only in the Q1 statements (note 18) and in management narrative. | Medium | CP-1, CP-5 | Check for a subsequent-events note or later 6-K. |

| G8 | Pending take-private review: the Q3 release states a Special Committee "provided interested parties with a final deadline of November 9, 2026". That date is after the cutoff 2026-11-05; outcome is unknown and must not be assumed. | Medium | CP-5 | Treat as an open subsequent event; no evidence after the cutoff may be used. |

| G9 | No credit ratings, quotes, market data or peer data are supplied (context ratings, quotes and valuation inputs are blank; blank is not zero). | Low for the minimum set | CP-5 | Supply if required. |

| G10 | Extraction fidelity not reviewed: sources are text extractions; no table-image or footnote-marker verification was done. The text inside each extracted file quotes a different sha256 for the underlying HTML than the pinned sha256 of the extracted file; the pinned values are used here and the difference is a transport artefact, not a content conflict. | Low | All | Spot-check key tables against filings downstream. |

| G11 | Inconsistent file date labels (period end for the statements, filing date for the releases) leave exact 6-K filing dates unsupplied for the statements. | Low | CP-5 | Confirm filing dates from EDGAR index if timing matters. |
### Conflicts

No conflict between a filed statement and a management document was found in the located core figures. Examples checked for agreement between release and statements: revenue "$2,155.3" and Adjusted EBITDA "$678.7" appear in both for Q3 2026. Net Leverage definitions differ from covenant definitions, which is a definitional difference to carry downstream, not a numeric conflict.
## Next module

CP-1 may proceed on the sources listed, with the limitations G1 to G11 carried forward, then CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 in the order the dependency planner sets. Next evidence action: obtain the FY2025 Form 40-F Exhibits 99.1 to 99.3, the credit agreements and indentures, and a post-November 5, 2026 check is not permitted for this run. DO NOT RUN is not recommended for any consumer.

| Other (subsidiary stand-alone facilities and other) | 528.0 | Subsidiary facilities mature September 21, 2030 and August 31, 2028 (page:13) |
| Subtotal | 11,696.4 | |
### Definitions and covenant text

- Revolving Credit Agreement financial maintenance covenants: "Total Net Funded Debt to Adjusted EBITDA" at most 5.00 to 1.00 "for a period of four complete fiscal quarters following completion of a Material Acquisition" and otherwise at most 4.50 to 1.00; "Interest Coverage Ratio must be equal to or greater than 3.00 to 1.00". Company states it "was in compliance with these covenants" at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025 (Q3 statements page:12, page:13). No ratio values are printed.

- Management Net Leverage (Q3 release page:14): 3.8x at September 30, 2026 versus 3.4x at December 31, 2025, using Run-Rate EBITDA of 2,988.0, which is trailing twelve months Adjusted EBITDA of 2,257.1 plus Run-Rate EBITDA Adjustments of 730.9 (management estimates). Earlier releases: 3.6x at March 31, 2026 (Q1 release page:13) and 4.0x at June 30, 2026 (Q2 release page:14). Guidance: "Net Leverage is estimated to be in the mid 3s by the end of 2026."

- Adjusted EBITDA adds back, for nine months 2026, share-based payments 87.0, transaction costs 70.6, acquisition, rebranding and other integration costs 27.3 and Founder/CEO remuneration 74.2, among others (Q3 statements page:15). Reported EBITDA before those adjustments is 1,203.4 for nine months 2026 versus Adjusted EBITDA 1,748.4 (Q3 release page:15).
### Latest-quarter changes (Q3 2026) as reported

- SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. acquired "On September 1, 2026" for total consideration of about 5,414.1 (share capital issued 4,334.8, cash paid 1,079.3); allocation is provisional, with goodwill 4,968.1 and other long-term liabilities 1,006.6 recorded (Q3 statements page:6, page:7).
- Term Loan B Facility entered August 28, 2026, 5.500% 2034 notes and 5.625% 2031 notes now outstanding; revolver drawn 868.0 versus 182.0 at June 30, 2026 (Q2 statements page:11).
- Q3 transaction costs 46.5 in Adjusted EBITDA and 80.4 in the cash flow reconciliation (Q3 release page:15, page:17).

- Guidance raised (Q3 release page:2, page:3): Adjusted EBITDA about 2,490 to 2,495 versus prior about 2,290; Adjusted Free Cash Flow about 1,020; net capex about 910; cash interest about 455. Management guidance, not a filed fact, and it excludes acquisitions not yet completed.
- A Special Committee is reviewing unsolicited take-private proposals with a stated deadline of November 9, 2026 (Q3 release page:1, page:6). This date is after the cutoff; outcome is unknown.
### Interpretation (evidence-based, no conclusion on creditworthiness)

- Leverage rose with the SECURE closing and the new financing. Reported debt before adjustments grew from 7,426.7 to 11,696.4 while the management leverage ratio moved from 3.4x to 3.8x, because the ratio's denominator includes 730.9 of management run-rate adjustments. On trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA alone, net debt to Adjusted EBITDA is about 5.05x (calculation below), which sits above the 4.50x general covenant level but is not a covenant calculation (covenant definitions are not supplied; the 5.00x step-up applies for four quarters after a Material Acquisition, and whether SECURE qualifies is not stated).

- Net loss from continuing operations in the nine months is driven by items below Adjusted EBITDA: foreign exchange loss 196.7, interest and other finance costs 482.9, and an equity-method loss, against Adjusted EBITDA of 1,748.4 (Q3 statements page:1).

- Cash generation: operating cash flow less purchase of property and equipment is thin for nine months 2026 (calculation below), and management's Adjusted Free Cash Flow of 484.9 depends on add-backs and a separate "incremental growth investments" addition of 182.4 (Q3 release page:18).
- Reported Q3 revenue growth of 27.2% includes the one month of SECURE and other acquisitions; the release states organic growth of 7.4%.
## Calculations
All inputs are printed in the cited pages; results are my arithmetic on those inputs and are not source-printed subtotals. CAD millions.
| Calculation | Inputs | Result | Note |
| Discrete quarters sum to nine months, revenue | 1,643.8 + 1,947.8 + 2,155.3 | 5,746.9 | Matches printed 9M 2026 |

| Net debt per management definition | 11,696.4 - 296.5 | 11,399.9 | Matches printed |
| Management Net Leverage reproduced | 11,399.9 / 2,988.0 | 3.82x | Printed 3.8x |
| Net debt to trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA | 11,399.9 / 2,257.1 | 5.05x | Not a covenant ratio; denominator includes only one month of SECURE |
| Increase in carrying debt since December 31, 2025 | 11,671.4 - 7,422.6 | 4,248.8 | |
| Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to interest and other finance costs | 678.7 / 179.4 | 3.78x | Not the covenant Interest Coverage Ratio (definition not supplied) |

The maturity buckets use carrying amounts of USD notes translated to CAD at the period-end rate, not principal, and treat "Other" as undistributed. They are a reader's aid, not a source-printed schedule.
## Gaps

- Not supplied: FY2025 audited statements, annual MD&A and annual information form (CP-0 G1). FY2025 values appear only as comparatives; December 31, 2025 balances were revised for the associate adjustment (Q3 statements page:8, page:9), so original FY2025 reported balances cannot be bridged.

- Not supplied: undrawn revolver availability and total liquidity. The revolver size is 2,000.0 plus 25.0 and drawn is 868.0, but letters of credit are partly under the revolver and partly under the EDC facility and the split is not printed, so availability is Not calculable.
- Not supplied: covenant ratio values, covenant definitions and whether the Material Acquisition step-up is in effect.
- Not supplied: Q4 2025 discrete quarter and FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation; trailing twelve months Adjusted EBITDA 2,257.1 and 1,985.0 are management figures.

- Not calculable: pro forma leverage with SECURE for a full year from filed statements alone; the only filed pro forma is revenue 6,905.3 and loss before income taxes 186.2 for nine months 2026 (Q3 statements page:8), without pro forma Adjusted EBITDA.
- Provisional accounting for SECURE: balances are subject to change in the measurement period.

- Presentation difference in 9M 2025 capex (893.1 versus 875.0) and in 9M 2025 interest and other finance costs between the Q1 statements and later comparatives (Q1 2025 interest and other finance costs 210.4 and cash flow add-back 212.0 in the Q1 statements); not reconciled here.
- Instrument-level principal in USD, guarantor, ranking and redemption terms are not supplied; carrying amounts are CAD translations.
- Text extraction only; table values were not verified against rendered filings.
## Next module

CP-1A (debt and liquidity) can proceed on the debt table, covenant text and Net Leverage definitions above; it should treat revolver availability, covenant values and indenture terms as open gaps. CP-2 can use the discrete quarter table, with the SECURE perimeter change flagged. CP-5 should treat the Special Committee deadline of November 9, 2026 as a post-cutoff open event.

Q3 2026 total collection is the largest line, then landfill and transfer | Documentary Fact | Q3 statements page:14 (note 10) | Collection is route-based and recurring; landfill and transfer carry vertical integration; intercompany elimination is material |

Q3 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA margin: Canada 35.7%, USA 33.8% versus 33.6% and 36.1% a year earlier | Documentary Fact | Q3 release page:14; Q3 statements page:15 | USA margin fell and Canada rose year on year; mix shifts with SECURE (Western Canada) |

| Organic growth and margin | Management states 7.4% organic revenue growth and "115 basis points" underlying margin expansion excluding M&A and diesel; reported Adjusted EBITDA margin 31.5% versus 31.6% | Management Language | Q3 release page:1, page:2 | Reported margin is flat while the underlying claim excludes M&A and diesel effects; underlying measure is not defined in a filed statement |

| Cost drivers | Cost of sales and SG&A are the two expense lines; diesel prices are cited as a headwind in guidance; depreciation includes landfill assets | Documentary Fact and Management Language | Q3 statements page:1, page:10; Q3 release page:3 | Fuel and disposal costs are the main pass-through exposures |

| Capital spending | Purchase of property and equipment in nine months 2026 (CP-1 table); guidance net capex about 910 for 2026; additional "incremental growth investments" mainly recycling are added back in management Adjusted Free Cash Flow | Documentary Fact and Management Language | Q3 statements page:4; Q3 release page:3, page:18 | Capex is a large call on operating cash flow; the add-back lowers conservatism of management free cash flow |

| Working capital | Change in non-cash working capital items was an outflow in the nine months, driven by trade and other receivables | Documentary Fact | Q3 statements page:17 (note 13) | Receivables growth with acquisition scale absorbs cash; SECURE receivables added at acquisition |

| Closure obligations | Closure and post-closure obligations of 1,503.8 at September 30, 2026; funded restricted assets of 38.9 | Documentary Fact | Q3 statements page:11 (note 6) | Long-dated, underfunded relative to the liability; a senior-claim-like obligation that grows with landfill acquisitions |

### Company profile
| Item | Fact | Category | Locator |

| Legal name and form | GFL Environmental Inc., "formed on March 5, 2020 under the laws of the Province of Ontario"; registered office Vaughan, Ontario; executive headquarters Miami Beach, Florida | Documentary Fact | Q3 statements page:4, page:5 (note 1) |

| Auditor | KPMG LLP | Documentary Fact | 40-F page:3 |

| Equity-method holdings | GFL Environmental Services (divested March 1, 2025, with a Call Option to repurchase the balance of the equity, fair value 95.0 at September 30, 2026) and RNG joint ventures | Documentary Fact | Q3 statements page:8, page:9 |

| Related parties | Tax obligations of the Founder and CEO on relocation paid by GFL in 2025 (33.5, recognized as a receivable); lease payments to related parties; transactions with Green Infrastructure Partners Inc. and GFL Environmental Services | Documentary Fact | Q3 statements page:19 (note 16) |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The dominant transaction is the SECURE Waste Infrastructure Corp. acquisition. The definitive agreement was entered "On April 12, 2026" (Q1 statements note 18, subsequent events); SECURE shareholders approved it in May and it went through regulatory review (Q2 release); GFL acquired 100% of the common shares "On September 1, 2026" (Q3 statements note 3, page:7). Documentary Fact: total consideration of about 5,414.1 satisfied by share capital of 4,334.8 and cash of 1,079.3; SECURE operates waste processing, industrial waste disposal and recycling in Western Canada and North Dakota; initial accounting is provisional and based on historical carrying values, so fair value adjustments could change goodwill, intangibles, property and the 1,006.6 of other long-term liabilities assumed. Mechanism: issuing 77,708,769 subordinate voting shares funded most of the price with equity, which limits the incremental debt, while the cash portion, repayment of acquired debt (if any, not stated in the supplied text) and transaction costs were funded with new debt. Credit implication: the equity-heavy structure moderates leverage growth, but the assumed obligations, closure liabilities of 271.8 and crude oil commitments broaden the senior and structurally senior claims ahead of or alongside the notes.

Alongside SECURE, GFL completed 13 businesses in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, each individually immaterial except SECURE, with combined purchase consideration for the others of 1,598.5 including 156.3 in shares (Q3 statements page:6). Management states year-to-date completed acquisitions generate "approximately $2 billion in annualized revenue" (Q3 release page:1) which is Management Language, not a filed fact.

New financing during 2026 (Documentary Fact, Q3 statements page:11 to page:14): a Term Loan B Facility entered August 28, 2026 maturing August 28, 2033 at SOFR plus 2.000%, carried at 1,418.8; 5.500% senior notes due February 1, 2034 (1,418.8) and 5.625% senior notes due July 1, 2031 (1,064.1), the latter with a cross-currency swap fixing the rate at 4.480% (entered June 25, 2026); a swap on the Term Loan B fixing the rate at 5.009%; the revolving credit agreement amended and restated through September 1, 2026 maturing April 29, 2030. The issuance of debt in the nine months was 6,795.9 and repayment 3,823.9 (cash flow statement, page:4). The use of proceeds is not stated in the supplied text beyond the statement that financing and acquisition activity occurred; the sources and uses of the SECURE financing are therefore partly Insufficient Information. The 6.750% 2031 notes had their collateral released and are no longer secured (note 7), which is a Documentary Fact bearing on the secured-unsecured balance of the capital structure; the indenture terms that permitted the release are not supplied.

Pending event, after the cutoff in resolution: in the third quarter a Special Committee of independent directors was formed to review unsolicited proposals to take the Company private, with updated proposals due November 9, 2026 (Q3 release page:1). Management Language states "There can be no assurance that the Company will receive any proposals". A take-private would raise change-of-control, leveraged buyout and covenant questions; indentures and credit agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity cannot be assessed. No outcome may be assumed.

Subsequent events: after March 31, 2026 GFL completed 5 acquisitions for about 1,437.6 (Q1 statements note 18); that disclosure was dated to the Q1 period and is not folded into Q1 figures. The Q3 statements contain no subsequent-events note in the extracted text.
### Governance and capital-allocation behaviour (issuer level, documented actions only)
| Action | Behaviour category | Mechanic | Evidence quality | Locator |

| Share repurchases: 300,000 shares in nine months 2026 and none in Q3 2026 versus 16,221,573 in nine months 2025; management says it will be "opportunistic" | Neutral or Mixed | Buybacks were suspended around the SECURE financing; cash is retained for debt service rather than returned; the NCIB authority remains up to 27,396,513 shares | High | Q3 statements page:16; Q3 release page:2 |

| Cash payment to Founder and CEO in lieu of restricted share units, 74.2 in nine months 2026, added back to Adjusted EBITDA | Neutral or Mixed | A cash outflow to an insider that management excludes from Adjusted EBITDA; it reduces cash available for debt service | High | Q3 statements page:15, page:16 |

| Debt-funded acquisitions, with equity as partial consideration | Neutral or Mixed | Leverage managed with equity issuance; acquisition appetite is evidenced by 13 deals plus SECURE this year, but no inference is drawn about future deals | High | Q3 statements page:6 |

| Collateral release on the 6.750% 2031 notes under the indenture terms | Insufficient Information on willingness | Release followed contractual terms (stated "pursuant to the terms of the indenture"); whether it was a creditor-adverse action cannot be judged without the indenture | Medium | Q3 statements page:12 |
| Special Committee review of take-private proposals | Insufficient Information | Control change could alter financial policy; no document shows terms | Medium | Q3 release page:1 |

| Reporting transparency: reconciliations of Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Free Cash Flow and Net Leverage are provided each quarter; guidance is quantified and raised three times | Supportive (disclosure) | Detailed non-IFRS bridges, though Run-Rate EBITDA includes management estimates | High | Q3 release page:14 to page:18 |

| Date | Event | Type | Locator |

### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability. Evidence: collection is the largest service line and pricing is described as "5.7% from core pricing" (Q3 release page:2). Mechanism: route-based collection revenue with pricing above inflation supports revenue visibility and margin resilience, while landfill and transfer volumes depend on construction and industrial activity. Implication: stable operating cash generation supports debt service tolerance, subject to the pricing claim being management's and to customer contract data being absent.

2. Leverage and acquisition integration. Evidence: Net Leverage 3.8x against 3.4x at December 31, 2025 (CP-1 handoff), and an unadjusted net-debt-to-trailing-Adjusted-EBITDA calculation above 5x in CP-1. Mechanism: SECURE contributes one month of EBITDA but all of its debt-funded cost and assumed liabilities, so reported coverage and leverage understate or overstate depending on whether run-rate adjustments of 730.9 are realised. Implication: refinancing and covenant headroom depend on the Material Acquisition step-up and on delivery of run-rate earnings; monitoring posture should be heightened until two full quarters including SECURE are reported.

3. Control and take-private uncertainty. Evidence: Special Committee and November 9, 2026 deadline (Q3 release page:1). Mechanism: a leveraged buyout or sponsor takeover could add debt or trigger change-of-control provisions in notes and credit facilities. Implication: monitoring item; no conclusion without indentures and credit agreements.

4. Cash-flow conversion. Evidence: management Adjusted Free Cash Flow of 484.9 for nine months against unadjusted operating cash flow less capex of 37.3 (CP-1 calculation). Mechanism: large add-backs (transaction costs, CEO remuneration, incremental growth investments) bridge the two. Implication: the committee should read management free cash flow alongside the unadjusted figure.

5. Structural claims. Evidence: closure obligations, performance bonds and letters of credit (Q3 statements page:11, page:18, page:19). Mechanism: asset retirement and surety obligations rank with operating claims and rise with landfill acquisitions. Implication: recovery prospects for unsecured noteholders depend on asset coverage after secured facilities and these obligations; no expected recovery outcome is given.
No logged conflict counters these translations beyond the conflicts section below.
## Calculations

No new calculation in this module. All figures are quoted from sources or referenced to the accepted CP-1 handoff (sha256 fd0b36c4541facbcfd57f1a25ee1d99854d60785b7b605c0414327e7191ae883): Net Leverage 3.8x and 3.4x, run-rate adjustments 730.9, unadjusted operating cash flow less capex 37.3 for nine months 2026, and net debt to trailing Adjusted EBITDA above 5x.

| Voting rights, holders and economic interest of the multiple voting shares and preferred shares not supplied | High | Control and willingness cannot be assessed; take-private dynamics depend on it | Supply the annual information form or proxy circular |
| Guarantor list, ranking, indentures, credit agreements, Term Loan B agreement | High | Legal capacity to prime, release collateral or incur debt cannot be judged | Supply the legal documents |

| SECURE financing sources and uses; debt assumed or repaid at closing; SECURE standalone financials | Medium | Net new debt attributable to SECURE cannot be isolated | Supply the acquisition circular or 6-K |
| Customer concentration, contract tenor, municipal share | Medium | Revenue durability by contract type | Supply the annual information form |
| Maturity schedule, revolver availability, covenant certificate and ratios | High | Refinancing and covenant headroom | Supply MD&A liquidity and compliance data |
| Add-back bridge detail beyond the printed reconciliation (Run-Rate EBITDA Adjustments of 730.9 composition) | Medium | Quality of the leverage ratio denominator | Supply management bridge |
| Ratings and market data not supplied | Low | Not needed for this module | Supply if required |
### Conflicts

No conflicting statements found across the supplied sources on transaction size or timing. One definitional difference is noted without reconciliation: Q3 total consideration for SECURE is about 5,414.1 in the statements, while the release speaks of year-to-date acquisitions generating "approximately $2 billion in annualized revenue", which measures a different quantity.

Fundamental credit synthesis (CP-2) for GFL Environmental Inc., as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot. Scope is the issuer's consolidated credit view in CAD from the accepted CP-0, CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs, with no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

## Findings
### Credit view

GFL Environmental Inc. is a resilient, price-led waste operator whose credit profile has weakened in the near term because the SECURE acquisition lifted carrying debt by CAD 4,248.8 million in nine months and management Net Leverage to 3.8x from 3.4x. The strongest support is steady collection and landfill earnings, with Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 678.7 million, a 31.5% margin, stated covenant compliance and mostly equity-funded purchase consideration. The weakest point is thin unadjusted cash generation: operating cash flow less capital spending was CAD 37.3 million over nine months, and net debt is 5.05x trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA. The outcome depends on SECURE earnings reaching the run-rate management assumes, headroom under the 5.00x acquisition covenant step-up, and the take-private review. The pack cannot confirm any of the three.

Confidence: Medium for the business view (Documentary Fact and Management Language mix); Low for forward leverage and covenant headroom (Insufficient Information on covenant values, run-rate bridge and liquidity).
### Key findings

1. GFL Environmental Inc. changed perimeter on September 1, 2026. SECURE was bought for about CAD 5,414.1 million, of which CAD 4,334.8 million was shares and CAD 1,079.3 million cash, but only one month of SECURE earnings is in the Q3 2026 statements. Reported leverage measures therefore carry the full debt and assumed liabilities against a partial earnings base. [CP-1; CP-1A transaction summary]

2. Leverage depends on management estimates. Net Leverage of 3.8x divides CAD 11,399.9 million of net debt by Run-Rate EBITDA of CAD 2,988.0 million, of which CAD 730.9 million (about a quarter) is management adjustment; on trailing reported Adjusted EBITDA of CAD 2,257.1 million the same net debt is 5.05x. The covenant ceiling is 5.00x for four fiscal quarters after a Material Acquisition and 4.50x otherwise, and covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom cannot be measured. Management guides to Net Leverage "in the mid 3s" by the end of 2026, a forward claim. [CP-1 calculations]

3. Operating performance is solid by management's account. Revenue grew 27.2% in Q3 2026, Adjusted EBITDA rose 26.8%, and the quarterly Adjusted EBITDA sequence of CAD 478.5, 591.2 and 678.7 million shows growth through the year, with core pricing near 6% stated by management. The reported margin was 31.5% against 31.6% a year earlier, so margin expansion exists only in management's underlying measure, which excludes M&A and diesel effects. [CP-1; CP-1A operating model]

4. Cash generation is weaker than the management free cash flow figure suggests. Management Adjusted Free Cash Flow was CAD 484.9 million for nine months, built from add-backs including CAD 104.5 million of transaction costs and CAD 74.2 million of cash paid to the Founder and CEO, plus CAD 182.4 million of incremental growth investments. Unadjusted operating cash flow less purchase of property and equipment was CAD 37.3 million. Cash interest rose to CAD 172.5 million in Q3 2026 from CAD 118.1 million a year earlier. [CP-1]

5. The debt stack is long-dated but large. Maturities begin in 2028 (CAD 2,128.2 million of notes), then 2029 (CAD 1,844.4 million), the revolver in 2030 (CAD 868.0 million drawn) and 2031 onward; there is almost no current maturity (CAD 14.2 million). The Term Loan B and revolver are secured, the 6.750% 2031 notes no longer have collateral, and the notes' guarantor and ranking terms are not supplied. [CP-1 debt table]

6. Fixed commitments and structurally senior-type claims grew. Closure and post-closure obligations reached CAD 1,503.8 million, performance bonds CAD 2,324.1 million, letters of credit CAD 535.1 million and new crude oil transportation commitments CAD 561.4 million from the SECURE addition. These rank with operating claims and shape loss-given-default mechanics without giving an expected recovery outcome. [CP-1; CP-1A]

7. Control and event risk is live. A Special Committee is reviewing unsolicited take-private proposals with a November 9, 2026 deadline, after the cutoff. A leveraged transaction could change financial policy and may engage change-of-control terms in debt documents that are not supplied. No outcome is assumed. [CP-1A]

8. Earnings quality is mixed. Net loss from continuing operations was CAD 409.8 million for nine months, driven by items outside Adjusted EBITDA (foreign exchange, financing costs, equity-method losses), and Adjusted EBITDA adds back share-based payments (CAD 87.0 million) and transaction costs. Several guided figures imply an unusually small Q4 step (see Calculations), which is unverified. [CP-1; CP-1 calculations]
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. First, the business is recurring and vertically integrated: collection is the largest revenue line and landfill and transfer add disposal control, which supports revenue visibility and margin resilience (Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model). Second, earnings momentum is real in the filed figures: Adjusted EBITDA grew in each quarter of 2026 and management raised guidance three times, though guidance is Management Language. Third, the acquisition was paid mainly with equity, issuing 77,708,769 subordinate voting shares, which limits the debt added by SECURE and leaves the revolver largely undrawn on a nominal basis relative to its size (the availability figure is not supplied). Fourth, the maturity profile has no material maturity before 2028 and interest on most notes is fixed in USD, with cross-currency swaps on the newest instruments (Documentary Fact). Fifth, covenant compliance is stated at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact), and disclosure of non-IFRS bridges is detailed each quarter (Analyst Interpretation).

Weaknesses. First, leverage on reported earnings is high and rests on run-rate estimates for the stated ratio, so the margin for error against a 5.00x covenant depends on an unsupplied definition (Analyst Interpretation). Second, cash conversion after capital spending and interest is thin and management free cash flow relies on add-backs (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation). Third, integration risk: provisional purchase accounting, a large goodwill balance (CAD 12,583.1 million, versus CAD 6,894.9 million at December 31, 2025) and a net loss from continuing operations mean book equity is largely acquired intangibles (Documentary Fact). Fourth, the take-private review and a dual-class structure with unspecified voting terms leave control and future leverage policy uncertain (Insufficient Information on voting rights). Fifth, commodity and fuel exposure: diesel is cited as a margin headwind, and the new crude oil commitments add a fixed obligation whose counterparties and tenor are not supplied (Management Language; Documentary Fact). Sixth, foreign exchange: most notes are USD while much revenue is CAD and USD, a mix that moves reported leverage and caused a CAD 196.7 million foreign exchange loss in nine months (Documentary Fact).
### Fundamental credit assessment

| Business risk | Moderate and supported by recurring collection and integrated disposal; customer concentration not supplied | Analyst Interpretation | Medium |
| Financial risk | Elevated after SECURE; reported leverage above covenant-style thresholds on trailing earnings, stated leverage mid-3s to high-3s on run-rate | Analyst Interpretation | Medium |
| Liquidity | Cash CAD 296.5 million, revolver drawn CAD 868.0 million, availability not supplied | Insufficient Information | Low |
| Governance and control | Public company; Special Committee review pending; control rights unspecified | Insufficient Information | Low |

| Overall | Business quality is solid, balance sheet stretched but with a long maturity runway; the view hinges on integration delivery | Analyst Interpretation | Medium for business, Low for forward leverage |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| SECURE integration shortfall | Run-rate adjustments of CAD 730.9 million underpin stated Net Leverage; shortfall raises effective leverage | Slower deleveraging, weaker covenant headroom | Material |
| Covenant step-up expiry | Ceiling steps from 5.00x to 4.50x after four fiscal quarters following the Material Acquisition | Pressure to delever or amend within a year | Material |
| Take-private transaction | Possible debt-funded transaction or change of control | Higher leverage, event risk on terms not supplied | Material |
| Cash conversion | Capex, cash interest and add-backs absorb operating cash flow | Limited free cash flow for debt reduction | Material |
| Refinancing | Large 2028 and 2029 maturities after heavy 2026 issuance | Market access dependence | Minor to Material |
| Fuel, commodity and crude commitments | Cost and fixed-commitment pressure | Margin and liquidity volatility | Minor |
| Foreign exchange | USD debt, mixed currency earnings, translation effects | Leverage swings | Minor |

CP-5 (report assembly) can use the credit view, key findings, strengths and weaknesses and risk table above.
